rail-states.caption: The session sidebar: every session with its program and folder, Running, Needs input and Done badges, an unread session in bold, and a bell per row.

rail-shortcuts.caption: The Shortcuts card in the sidebar lists the keyboard shortcuts: copy on release, paste, interrupt or copy, newline, new session, changes and search.

new-session.caption: Starting a new session: the name field shows the name it will get if left empty.

new-session-key.caption: Ctrl+Shift+L made a new session with a dated name and opened it.

session-sheet.caption: The rename sheet for a session: a display name, the tmux name, and Kill.

search.caption: Searching the terminal's history with Ctrl+Shift+F: matches are highlighted and counted.

key-pill.caption: A path printed in the terminal becomes a link under the pointer; the key pill at the top right holds the mic, files, browser and report keys.

prompt-chips.caption: A session waiting on a yes/no question: one-tap answer chips appear above the terminal.

settings-connection.caption: Settings, Connection: the computer chooser open with two computers and Add another computer, above the address, pairing code and names.

settings-pair.caption: Settings, Connection: the QR code another phone or laptop scans to pair with this computer.

settings-browser.caption: Settings, Connection, Browser: stream every tab from the computer's Chrome, and clear its browsing data.

settings-dictation.caption: Settings, Dictation: the speech engine choice and the corrections dictation has learned.

settings-keys.caption: Settings, Keys: text size buttons for the terminal and sidebar, and every keyboard shortcut.

settings-appearance.caption: Settings, Appearance: app theme, terminal colour schemes and the box to paste your own.

settings-about.caption: Settings, About: the app and server versions, the Update server button, the debug log switch and Report a problem.

update-failed.caption: After an update that did not take, Settings, About offers Type it for me to put the retry command in a terminal.

theme-menu.caption: The theme button in the header: light, dark or follow the system.

report.caption: Report a problem, with the diagnostics that will be sent shown before sending.

first-run.caption: First run: step one is the command to run on the computer, with the Tailscale steps above it.

explorer.caption: The file browser docked beside the terminal, opened on the session's own folder.

explorer-grid.caption: Grid view in the file browser, with picture previews for images.

explorer-view-menu.caption: The layout pop-up: list or grid, sorted by name, date or size.

explorer-branch.caption: The branch pop-up in the path bar: read another branch's files without checking it out.

explorer-path.caption: Typing a path in the file browser's path bar, with folder suggestions.

explorer-more.caption: The More menu in a docked pane: open another pane in this column, including a second of the same kind.

explorer-actions.caption: Right-clicking a folder in the file browser: Download, Rename and Delete.

explorer-add.caption: The + menu in the file browser: new file, new folder, upload.

explorer-drag.caption: Dragging a file onto a folder in the file browser to move it there.

editor.caption: A file open in the editor beside the terminal, with Wrap, Vim and Save in its bar.

markdown.caption: A Markdown file in the reader: formatted text, a formula and a task list.

viewer.caption: A picture opened from the file browser, with the viewer expanded over the terminal; pinch, drag or double-tap to zoom.

diff.caption: The Changes pane (Ctrl+Shift+G): changed files with stage and discard buttons, and the diff with a keep or undo control on each block.

diff-untracked.caption: The Untracked tab of the Changes pane: files git has never seen, listed apart from tracked changes.

browser.caption: The browser pane showing a dev server on the computer: tabs, the address field, bookmarks bar, and the stream key.

browser-more.caption: The browser pane's More menu: another pane in this column, and zoom in, out or actual size.

two-panes.caption: Two tools stacked beside the terminal: the file browser above the browser, with the seam between them.

two-explorers.caption: Two file browsers in one column, each on its own folder.
